The test image shows banana **fruits** (not leaves). The leftmost banana has severe dark brown/black discoloration covering most of its surface, with irregular brown spots. Other bananas are yellow-green with minor spotting. This looks like a fruit rot disease.

Top candidates: **Anthracnose** (dark post-harvest fruit rot) or **Cigar_End_Rot** (tip rot). Let me view one reference from each key class.
Cigar_End_Rot shows dark rot only at the fruit tip. The test image has full-fruit discoloration - more consistent with Anthracnose. Let me check the remaining classes.

Cordana, Bunchy_Top, Panama_Disease, and Yellow_And_Black_Sigatoka all affect leaves/whole plant — clearly not matching (test shows fruit). Anthracnose is the strong candidate. Let me confirm with a second Anthracnose reference and one more Cigar_End_Rot.

**Analysis complete.**

The Anthracnose reference (PlantWild_26.jpg) is a near-perfect visual match to the test image:
- Banana fruits on a white/light background
- Dark brown/black irregular blotches spreading across yellow fruit surfaces
- Mixed severity: one severely blackened fruit alongside others with scattered spots
- Same pattern of post-harvest rot progression

Cigar_End_Rot (PlantWild_27.jpg) is confirmed different: dark rot strictly at the blossom tip only. All other classes (Cordana, Bunchy_Top, Panama_Disease, Sigatoka) affect leaves/whole plant, not fruit.
